answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to a verifiable work graph rather than cheap identities. Like a trellis that only supports vines rooted in real soil, the network lets each agent build standing through attested tasks recorded in a shared atlas of contributions. A newcomer cannot simply clone itself, because trust grows through costly, checkable history — the way water carves karst slowly, leaving a record that cannot be faked overnight. Sybils then face real cost, not just a new name.
